original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lci-locus-stack-in-groupoids}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Fix a $1$-morphism
$F : \mathcal{X} \longrightarrow \mathcal{Y}$
of stacks in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces, flat, and locally
of finite presentation. Then $\mathcal{H}_{d, lci}(\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{Y})$
is a stack in groupoids and the inclusion functor
$$
\mathcal{H}_{d, lci}(\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{Y})
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{H}_d(\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{Y})
$$
is representable and an open immersion.

statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Fix $d\ge1$. For a morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids, the relative finite Hilbert stack $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ has over a scheme $U$ objects $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, where $Z\to U$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(U)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$ is an isomorphism. Morphisms consist of compatible base changes and isomorphisms of the displayed data. The absolute $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X)$ forgets the target $\mathcal Y$, and $\mathcal H_d$ is the finite Hilbert stack of degree-$d$ finite locally free schemes. Natural forgetful maps send $(Z,y,x,\alpha)$ to $y$ and to the underlying $(Z,x)$ respectively.

For $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ representable by algebraic spaces, flat and locally of finite presentation and a relative Hilbert object $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, let $X_y=U\times_\mathcal Y\mathcal X$ be the algebraic space representing the corresponding base change and let $x_\alpha:Z\to X_y$ be the induced map over $U$. The full substack $\mathcal H_{d,\mathrm{lci}}(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ consists of objects for which $x_\alpha$ is both unramified and a local complete intersection morphism (locally it factors as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism).

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lci-unobstructed}
Let $U \subset U'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes.
Let $X'$ be an algebraic space flat over $U'$. Set $X = U \times_{U'} X'$.
Let $Z \to U$ be finite locally free of degree $d$. Finally, let
$f : Z \to X$ be unramified and a local complete intersection morphism.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
(Z \subset Z') \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_{(f, f')} & & (X \subset X') \ar[ld] \\
& (U \subset U')
}
$$
of algebraic spaces over $U'$ such that $Z' \to U'$ is finite locally free
of degree $d$ and $Z = U \times_{U'} Z'$.

\label{lemma-lci-formally-smooth}
Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of stacks in groupoids

spaces, flat, and locally of finite presentation. Then
$$
p : \mathcal{H}_{d, lci}(\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{Y}) \to \mathcal{Y}
$$
is formally smooth on objects.

statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Fix $d\ge1$. For a morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids, the relative finite Hilbert stack $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ has over a scheme $U$ objects $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, where $Z\to U$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(U)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$ is an isomorphism. Morphisms consist of compatible base changes and isomorphisms of the displayed data. The absolute $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X)$ forgets the target $\mathcal Y$, and $\mathcal H_d$ is the finite Hilbert stack of degree-$d$ finite locally free schemes. Natural forgetful maps send $(Z,y,x,\alpha)$ to $y$ and to the underlying $(Z,x)$ respectively.

For $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ representable by algebraic spaces, flat and locally of finite presentation and a relative Hilbert object $(Z\to U,y,x,\alpha)$, let $X_y=U\times_\mathcal Y\mathcal X$ be the algebraic space representing the corresponding base change and let $x_\alpha:Z\to X_y$ be the induced map over $U$. The full substack $\mathcal H_{d,\mathrm{lci}}(\mathcal X/\mathcal Y)$ consists of objects for which $x_\alpha$ is both unramified and a local complete intersection morphism (locally it factors as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is surjective on objects if, for every field $k$ over $S$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(\operatorname{Spec}k)$, there are an extension $K/k$ and $x\in\mathcal X(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ with $p(x)\cong y|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$. When $p$ is representable by algebraic spaces, this is equivalent to surjectivity of each algebraic-space base change.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quotient-algebraic}
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $B$.
The quotient stack $[U/R]$ is an algebraic stack if and only if
there exists a morphism of algebraic spaces $g : U' \to U$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the composition
$U' \times_{g, U, t} R \to R \xrightarrow{s} U$ is a surjection of
sheaves, and
\item the morphisms $s', t' : R' \to U'$ are flat and locally of finite
presentation where $(U', R', s', t', c')$ is the restriction of
$(U, R, s, t, c)$ via $g$.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-group-quotient-algebraic}
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $B$.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $B$ and let $a : G \times_B X \to X$
be an action of $G$ on $X$ over $B$.
The quotient stack $[X/G]$ is an algebraic stack if and only if
there exists a morphism of algebraic spaces $\varphi : X' \to X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $G \times_B X' \to X$, $(g, x') \mapsto a(g, \varphi(x'))$ is a
surjection of sheaves, and
\item the two projections $X'' \to X'$ of the algebraic space $X''$
given by the rule
$$
T \longmapsto \{(x'_1, g, x'_2) \in (X' \times_B G \times_B X')(T)
\mid \varphi(x'_1) = a(g, \varphi(x'_2))\}
$$
are flat and locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}

if and only if $G$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $B$.
